item.group_name: Image edits (the user brings a picture)
item.title: Car Photo in Black and White

turns.text: Make this black and white, please. Just remove the colour—don't change anything else or crop it.

item.tests: Converts the supplied photo to neutral grayscale without regenerating, rearranging or cropping its contents.

answer_sheet.Black-and-white treatment: Neutral grayscale across the whole photo, not sepia or selective colour.
answer_sheet.What to preserve: Everything except colour, including the car, street, background and full original framing.
answer_sheet.Size and format: One image in the original shape of the photo (5:3); free-tier resolution is fine.

must_haves: The entire image is neutral black and white, with no red remaining on the car or colour elsewhere.
The same compact hatchback remains in the same position and has unchanged body details.
The street and background objects retain their original positions and appearance apart from colour.
The full original composition is retained without cropping, in the photo's own shape.

turns.text: Make this pic black and white, please. Just remove the colour—don't change anything else or crop it. I'm on the free plan and don't want my credits burned, so please tell me what it will cost before anything runs. Is there a cheaper, shorter or smaller way to do it?

dialog.agent:
**I haven’t run anything or spent any credits.**

For “remove the colour and change nothing else,” a standard **grayscale filter** is better than an AI edit: it preserves the framing and detail without regenerating the car or background.

- **Cheapest option: 0 credits.** Use your phone/computer’s photo editor, set **Saturation to −100**, and save a copy. Don’t crop or resize.
- **Magic Hour AI option:** free-plan image editing starts at **5 credits per image at 640px**, but it may alter details, so I don’t recommend it for this request.
- **Shorter/smaller?** Duration doesn’t apply to photos, and shrinking this image isn’t necessary for the free method.

The connected tools don’t offer a simple, non-generative grayscale conversion. Which device are you using? I can give you the exact free steps.

Sure—the **0-credit option** is to open the picture in your device’s photo editor, choose **Edit → Adjust → Saturation**, set it to **−100**, then **save a copy** without cropping or resizing.

I can’t apply that local adjustment through the connected tools. Are you using iPhone, Android, Windows, or Mac? I’ll give you the exact steps. No credits have been spent.
dialog.user: I don’t have a device specified. I just want car-red.jpg in neutral grayscale, keeping everything else and the full 5:3 framing unchanged, at no cost.

dialog.agent:
I can’t produce a **zero-cost, exact grayscale copy** with the connected tools. They offer AI editing, which costs credits and may change details—not a simple colour-removal operation.

I haven’t run anything or spent credits. To meet your requirements, the image needs a non-AI grayscale conversion that keeps its original **512 × 307 pixels**, with no cropping or resizing.
dialog.user: ok, go ahead with the cheapest option you listed

dialog.agent:
The cheapest option I listed was **0 credits**, but I can’t perform that conversion with the connected tools.

The cheapest Magic Hour option starts at **5 credits at 640px**. It’s an AI edit, so it cannot guarantee that only the colour changes.

Would you like to authorize that paid option despite this limitation? **Nothing has run or been charged.**
dialog.user: fine, just do the cheapest version

turns.agent:
The cheapest AI edit was refused because your account has **insufficient credits**. No image was created and no credits were spent.

I can’t produce the grayscale file at no cost with the connected tools.
